words.def: have a particular job
words.ex: Nam works as a designer in Manchester.
words.scene: Nam as a designer at a big screen with colour swatches and drawing tablet.

words.def: it is your job to take care of something
words.ex: Claire is responsible for the whole team.
words.scene: Claire standing in front of her small team (Nam, Tom, two others) with a clipboard, leading them.

words.def: spend time doing or improving something
words.ex: Tom is working on a new website.
words.scene: Tom concentrating on building a website on his laptop, sticky notes around the screen.

words.def: you need this much time to do something
words.ex: It takes twenty minutes to walk to work.
words.scene: Nam walking from a small house to an office building along a path, with a big clock above the path showing 20 minutes as a coloured arc.

words.def: use time for an activity
words.ex: He spent an hour logging in to his new laptop.
words.scene: Nam at a laptop trying to log in (padlock on screen), an hourglass beside him almost empty – an hour spent.

words.def: every day = each day (adverb); everyday = normal, usual (adjective)
words.ex: I drink coffee every day. It's an everyday thing.
words.scene: Left: a wall calendar with every day ticked and a coffee cup; right: simple everyday clothes (t-shirt, jeans) on a chair – each day vs normal things.

words.def: shows a surprising contrast: A is true, but B is also true
words.ex: Although he was tired, he helped Mr Patel.
words.scene: Nam looks very tired (droopy eyes, small zz shapes) BUT still carries a big box up the stairs for Margaret – show tired + helping in one scene.

words.def: a stronger 'although'
words.ex: Even though it was raining, they went for a walk.
words.scene: Heavy rain falling, yet two friends walk happily together under umbrellas, smiling – rain + still happy.

words.def: but (starts a new sentence, followed by a comma)
words.ex: The answer sounded right. However, it was wrong.
words.scene: Left: a cute robot proudly pointing at a board with an answer; right: the board shows a big red X – it sounded right, but it was wrong.

words.def: but (a little surprising)
words.ex: The café is small, yet it's always full.
words.scene: A tiny café building that is completely full of people inside and a queue outside – small, yet full.

words.def: not A – B instead
words.ex: He didn't text. Rather, he called.
words.scene: Left: a phone with a chat bubble crossed out; right: Nam talking on the phone, smiling – not texting, calling instead.

words.def: if … not
words.ex: I can't sleep unless the room is dark.
words.scene: Two panels: left: bedroom with lamp on, Nam awake and annoyed in bed; right: same room dark with moon in window, Nam sleeping peacefully.

words.def: saying the same idea again, more clearly
words.ex: It's a moving target. In other words, the goal keeps changing.
words.scene: Two panels showing the same idea twice: left: an archery target on wheels rolling away; right: a goal flag that keeps jumping to new places with dotted arrows.

words.def: quickly use an idea or chance with great interest
words.ex: Reporters seized upon the new study.
words.scene: Reporters with microphones rushing eagerly towards a scientist holding a new report.

words.def: stop doing something; give up
words.ex: I nearly packed it in, but I kept practising.
words.scene: Two panels: left: a person at a piano, frustrated, about to close the lid; right: the same person still playing, determined.

words.def: How are you? (friendly)
words.ex: “Hi Nam, how's it going?” – “Good, thanks!”
words.scene: Tom waving hello to Nam in an office corridor, both smiling.

words.def: until now, everything is OK
words.ex: “How's the new job?” – “So far so good.”
words.scene: Nam on his first day at a bright office, giving a thumbs up, with a short path behind him (progress) and the path ahead still long.

words.def: tell me
words.ex: If you need anything, just let me know.
words.scene: Tom at the office smiling and pointing to himself with an open hand, Nam asking with a small question-mark shape bubble (no letters).

words.def: slowly learn how to do something
words.ex: It takes a while to get the hang of the new system.
words.vi: quen tay, nắm được cách làm
words.scene: Two panels: left: Nam wobbling nervously on a bicycle; right: Nam riding confidently and smiling.

words.def: I would really like
words.ex: I'd love another coffee.
words.scene: Jess at a café counter offering a cup of coffee, Nam with sparkling happy eyes reaching for it.

words.def: starting a new, small topic
words.ex: By the way, where's the kitchen?
words.scene: Claire and Nam talking at an office desk with documents; Nam turns and points to a small kitchen door with a coffee cup sign (no text) – switching to a new small topic.

words.def: on the other side, facing
words.ex: The tram stop is opposite the church.
words.scene: A street with a tram stop on one side and a church directly across the street on the other side, a dotted line connecting them across the road.

words.def: right beside
words.ex: The phone shop is next to the bank.
words.scene: A phone shop and a bank standing right side by side on a street.

words.def: change direction
words.ex: Go out of the café and turn left.
words.scene: Nam coming out of a café door at a street corner, a big curved arrow showing him turning left.

words.def: walk by something without stopping
words.ex: Go past the park and you'll see it.

words.def: enter / leave a bus, tram or train
words.ex: Get on at Hope Street and get off at Market Street.

words.def: you need ten minutes to walk there
words.ex: The station is a ten-minute walk from here.
words.scene: Nam walking along a street with a dotted path to a building, a small stopwatch icon showing a 10-minute sector.

words.def: it's very easy to find
words.ex: The church is huge. You can't miss it.
words.scene: A huge church at the end of a small street, very easy to see, Nam looking at it with a surprised smile.

words.def: I understand (informal)
words.ex: “Turn left at the church.” – “Got it.”
words.scene: Jess pointing left towards a church on a street map gesture, Nam nodding with an OK hand sign.

words.def: start living in a new home
words.ex: Nam moved in yesterday.

words.def: feel comfortable, as if you belong
words.ex: After a week, he felt at home in the café.

words.def: I should (or something bad may happen)
words.ex: It's late – I'd better go.
words.scene: Late evening, a wall clock at 11, Nam putting on his jacket and hurrying to the door.

words.def: very, very boring
words.ex: The meeting was like watching grass grow.

words.def: boring because it is long and the same again and again
words.ex: Filling in forms is tedious.

words.def: always busy and moving
words.ex: She's always on the go – work, gym, friends.

words.w: don't let the grass grow under your feet
words.def: don't wait – act now and keep moving
words.ex: Don't let the grass grow under your feet – apply today!
words.ipa: /dəʊnt let ðə ɡræs ɡrəʊ ˈʌndə jə fiːt/
words.ipa_us: /doʊnt let ðə ɡræs ɡroʊ ˈʌndər jə fiːt/

words.def: all the things you have to do
words.ex: I have a lot on my plate this week.
words.scene: A big dinner plate on a table piled with tiny objects: a laptop, papers, a phone, a calendar – too many things to do.

words.def: feeling there is too much and you can't manage
words.ex: He felt overwhelmed by all the emails.

words.def: try to do too many things, so nothing goes well
words.ex: She's spread herself too thin with three jobs.
words.scene: A person trying to hold many things at once – juggling a briefcase, books, a theatre mask and a phone – looking stressed.

words.w: bite off more than you can chew
words.def: try to do more than is possible
words.ex: I bit off more than I could chew with this project.
words.ipa: /baɪt ɒf mɔː ðən jə kən tʃuː/
words.ipa_us: /baɪt ɔf moːr ðən jə kən tʃuː/

words.def: doing several things at the same time
words.ex: Multitasking can make you slower.

words.def: give more time to finish
words.ex: The teacher extended the deadline by a week.
words.scene: A calendar where the red deadline circle moves one week later along a dotted arrow, a teacher smiling and students relieved.

words.def: start something
words.ex: We kicked off the project with a meeting.

words.def: a promise to yourself to reach a goal
words.ex: My resolution is to listen to English every day.
words.vi: quyết tâm, mục tiêu tự hứa

words.def: give a task to someone else, or decide later
words.ex: I'll punt that decision until next week.
words.scene: Tom passing a big box of work papers to a colleague with a relieved face.

words.def: wait until later to talk about it
words.ex: Let's table it until Monday.
words.scene: Three colleagues at a meeting table; one puts a folder aside onto a 'later' tray, calendar showing next Monday highlighted.

words.def: change the rules or goal so success is harder
words.ex: The boss keeps moving the goalposts.
words.scene: A football pitch: a player about to kick while two people carry the goalposts further away.

words.def: a goal that changes all the time
words.ex: The budget is a moving target.
words.scene: An archer aiming at a target that is on wheels and rolling away, with motion lines.

words.def: what is left
words.ex: I'll read the rest of the story tonight.
words.scene: A book half read with a bookmark, on a bed at night with the moon in the window – reading the rest tonight.

words.def: think of an idea or a plan
words.ex: Can you come up with a name for our new puppy?
words.scene: A girl at a kitchen table holds a pencil and smiles as a light bulb glows above her notebook, with a small puppy at her feet.

words.def: used before you say what you really think
words.ex: To be honest, I didn't like the film very much.
words.scene: Two friends sit on a sofa after watching a film on TV, one with a small shrug and an apologetic smile, popcorn on the table.

words.def: not be able to speak (or only whisper) because your throat is tired or ill
words.ex: He lost his voice after shouting at the football match.
words.scene: A man in a football scarf stands in a stadium with his hand on his throat and his mouth open, the crowd cheering behind him.

words.def: be very excited to do something
words.ex: I can't wait to see the sea next week.
words.scene: A child with a suitcase and sunhat jumps with joy by the front door, with a picture of a beach on the wall.

words.def: not broken; still works well
words.ex: I bought a used laptop in good condition for half the price.
words.scene: A smiling person holds a clean, shiny old laptop on a wooden table.

words.def: contact someone by phone or message
words.ex: Get in touch with me if you need a lift to the station.
words.scene: A woman holds a phone to her ear and waves with her other hand outside a station.

words.def: asking if something is not sold or taken yet
words.ex: Hello, is the room still available for next month?
words.scene: A man holds a phone and looks at a small empty room with a bed, an open door and sunlight.

words.def: visit someone at their home
words.ex: Why don't you come round on Sunday for lunch?
words.scene: A woman opens a front door with a big smile to a friend holding flowers.

words.def: I decide to buy it
words.ex: That jacket fits perfectly. I'll take it.
words.scene: A customer holds a warm jacket up in a small shop and hands money to the shop owner.

words.def: immediately, with no waiting
words.ex: When the phone rang, she answered it straight away.
words.scene: A woman jumps up from a sofa and picks up a ringing phone on a side table.

words.def: stop trying
words.ex: It was hard to learn the guitar, but he didn't give up.
words.scene: A young man sits with a guitar, tired but determined, practising again.

words.def: in that time in the past, not now
words.ex: Phones were huge back then.
words.scene: An old man points at a faded photo of a street full of old cars and children in 1980s clothes.

words.def: start to know people and like them
words.ex: It's easy to make friends at a dance class.
words.scene: Three strangers laugh together while holding paper cups at a class table.

words.def: accept an invitation or chance
words.ex: I said yes to the party even though I was tired.
words.scene: A young man holds a party invitation card and nods with a smile.

words.def: take care of someone or something
words.ex: My neighbour looks after my plants when I travel.
words.scene: A woman waters pot plants on a neighbour's windowsill while holding a spare key.

words.def: relax and don't hurry or worry
words.ex: Let's take it easy this afternoon and watch a film.
words.scene: Two friends lying on a sofa with tea and a blanket on a rainy afternoon.

words.def: watch so nothing bad happens
words.ex: Can you keep an eye on my bag while I buy a drink?
words.scene: A woman at a cafe table looking at a backpack on the chair while her friend queues at the counter.

words.def: walk with a new person and show them a place
words.ex: My cousin showed me around her school on my first day.
words.scene: A girl pointing along a school corridor while a new boy follows her.

words.def: to be safe, because something might happen
words.ex: Take an umbrella, just in case it rains.
words.scene: A man putting an umbrella into his backpack on a sunny morning with grey clouds far away.

words.def: in the opposite direction from the correct one
words.ex: We drove the wrong way and ended up in a small village.
words.scene: A car driving right while a big road sign with an arrow points left.

words.def: used to + verb = a past habit that stopped; be used to + -ing = it's normal for you now
words.ex: Sam used to take the bus, but now she's used to walking in the rain.
words.scene: Split scene: on the left a man frowning under a small umbrella in heavy rain; on the right the same man smiling and walking happily in the rain.
